parts:
the best option is to do the parameterisation and the priors, so that
you can actually specify this in the model. this is what's behind

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/makemyprior/index.html

and the relevant publication

Fuglstad, Geir-Arne, Ingeborg Gullikstad Hem, Alexander Knight, Håvard
Rue, and Andrea Riebler. 2020. “Intuitive Joint Priors for Variance
Parameters.” Bayesian Anal. 15 (4): 1109–37.

please check this out if this what you need.



Also the model

inla.doc("bym2")

is an example of a similar construction.



Best
H


On Sun, 2023-04-09 at 07:48 -0700, newer wrote:
> Hi all，
> I am new to INLA.
> In a word:
> Iencountered trouble when using "copy". I wonder if there is a way to
> control the contribution of both models to the final space effect. 
> In details, 
> I used  prevalence data(point-referenced)to build spde model. And , I
> used incidence data (area data, provincial level ) to build the spde
> mode in the same region to provide some spatial information. Due to 
> point-referenced data are insufficient to build to a steady sped
> model.  However,  area data  contributes almost 2/3  random effect in
> the final result. I would like to know if is there a method to control
> the degree of impact of   area data . (For example, I want to have 10%
> of the contribution form area data and 90% from point data in the
> results of spatial effects.)  
> Here is my formula:
> gaus.prior <- list(prior="gaussian", param = c(1,2))
> for1 <- c("-
> 1","Intercept","f(field,model=spde,hyper=hyper)","f(loc_id,model='iid'
> )")
> ###field represents modeling point data
> for2 <- c("b0","f(field_inc ,copy='field',fixed=T
> ,hyper=list(theta=gaus.prior))")
> ###field_inc represents modeling area data
> formula <- as.formula(paste(“y" ~ ，paste(paste(for1, collapse="+"),
> paste(paste(for2, collapse="+"), sep="+")))
> result <- inla(formula,
>                data=inla.stack.data(stack.full,spde=spde),
>                family=c("binomial","poisson"),
>                Ntrials=inla.stack.data(stack.full)$Ntrials,
>                E=inla.stack.data(stack.full)$E,
>                control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE,
>                                       A=inla.stack.A(stack.full),
>                                       quantiles=c(0.025,0.5,0.975),
>                                       link=link),
>                control.compute = list(dic=TRUE,config=TRUE,cpo=TRUE),
>                control.inla = list(int.strategy = "eb"),
>                verbose=T)
